Roblox claims it has made changes to its popular children's app to protect children from bad actors, but regulators say those protections don't go far enough.

The agency identified four major shortcomings, including the ability for adults to send friend requests to children without parental approval...

Australia's eSafety Commissioner today revealed vulnerabilities found during testing:

  • Adults could send friend requests to young Australian children without parental or guardian consent;
  • Children and adults could view and reply to each other's posts on forums outside the gaming environment without parental or guardian consent;
  • A child's connections list was visible to anyone on the Roblox platform;
  • A child's profile and bio – including non-sensitive profile information such as account name, number and names of connections, avatar image, and interests – was visible to anyone on the Roblox platform, with no ability to limit who could see this information

The agency said Roblox has agreed to implement stronger measures within three months:

  • Preventing adults from contacting unknown children without parental consent
  • Strengthening child account settings so they are private by default
  • Providing easy-to-use reporting mechanisms and notifying users of complaint outcomes
  • Engaging an independent third-party auditor to evaluate the effectiveness of its safety measures, including the deployment of age estimation measures

Roblox has more than 380 million active users, the majority of whom are under 16.
